meaning.evidence: "November 22 through December 20, 2024" preserves the original year rather than correcting it; all office, price, tag and eligibility details survive.

sense.evidence: "first dibs" correctly expresses priority; "skinny little trees" conveys small diameter.

authenticity.evidence: "Give us a ring" and "find a feed" are natural Australian expressions.

register.evidence: "cos it matters", "does the bush a good turn" and "find a feed" make the body noticeably broader than the requested light level 2.

tone.evidence: "Have a good read of the overview" maintains the practical advisory purpose.

flow.evidence: "That depends on the weather and the supply" reads as a clear spoken explanation.

variety.evidence: "Chrissy" recurs throughout almost every tree reference, making the diminutive conspicuous.

essence.evidence: "One tag covers a tree up to 5 inches" retains the administrative detail and forest-health explanation that distinguish the notice.

meaning.evidence: "November 13, 2025" and "November 22 through December 20, 2024" preserve both dates, and all fees and tag thresholds remain.

sense.evidence: "Get in touch with us" preserves the unrestricted contact instruction, and "first priority" conveys the allocation rule.

authenticity.evidence: "Have a look here" and "does the forest some good too" sound natural and unforced.

tone.evidence: "you’ll need another tag" keeps the instruction clear and suitably serious.

flow.evidence: "Buying through recreation.gov adds a $2.50 service fee" is concise and easily read aloud.

variety.evidence: "Have a look", "Get in touch" and "for instance" vary the transitions without repeated slang.

essence.evidence: "Local forest health experts pick out areas" retains the distinctive explanatory ending and practical notice structure.

B.summary: Faithful, clear notice with the right light Australian weight.

meaning.evidence: "Year 4 kids" recasts a US fourth-grade eligibility category as an Australian school-year label, while dates, fees and dimensions otherwise remain.

sense.evidence: "first dibs" correctly expresses priority and "patches of feed" reasonably conveys forage.

authenticity.evidence: "have a proper read" and "does the bush a good turn" are credible local speech.

register.evidence: "just pop in", "heads up" and "skinny little trees" give the whole notice a broader voice than level 2 asks for.

tone.evidence: "Make sure you have a proper read" preserves the practical advisory force.

flow.evidence: "Buy one online through recreation.gov and there's an extra $2.50 service fee on top." is smooth explanatory speech.

variety.evidence: "Chrissie" repeats in most references to the trees and permits, drawing attention to itself.

essence.evidence: "Anything taller than 10 feet and/or wider than 5 inches needs an extra tag" retains the unusually specific permit mechanics and the forest-benefit ending.

problems.why: Eligibility belongs to a US programme; replacing the school-system category with Year 4 can mislead a reader applying an Australian label.

C.summary: Readable and complete in most respects, but too broad for level 2 and with a less exact eligibility label.
